units.title: Our first bowling game
units.alignmentNote: Complete original ten-gap passage with seven supplied-word and three one-word gaps. Source is a level/family reference only.

materials.title: Our first bowling game
materials.text:
My cousins invited me to go bowling during the holiday. I had never played before, so I listened ____1____ (careful) when the staff explained the equipment. We borrowed suitable shoes and followed the rules for staying behind the marked line.

The first ball I tried was too heavy ____2____ me to hold comfortably. A staff member helped me choose another one. It was ____3____ (light), and I could control it more easily without trying to copy my older cousin's choice.

Our names appeared on a screen above the lane. I watched the numbers change after each turn, but did not understand all the marks. My cousin explained one symbol ____4____ appeared when a player knocked down every pin with the first ball.

On my third turn, the ball moved towards the side almost immediately. I felt disappointed, but everyone else had made mistakes too. My cousin suggested ____5____ (watch) where I began rather than only staring at the pins.

The next attempt was better. I did not win the game, but I hit more pins than before. The screen recorded each of my ____6____ (turn), so I could see the change instead of judging everything by the final total.

After the game, we returned the shoes and thanked the staff for ____7____ (they) help. Our lane ____8____ (prepare) for the next group while we collected our bags. I left with ____9____ better idea of the sport and looked forward to ____10____ (try) again. Next time, I would ask about the scoring before the first turn rather than waiting until everyone was cheering at a symbol I could not read.

questions.prompt: Fill gap 1 with the correct form of careful.
questions.explanation: Carefully modifies listened. Careful is adjective and carefulness noun.

questions.prompt: Fill gap 2 with one appropriate word.
questions.explanation: Too heavy for me to hold uses for to introduce the person in the infinitive clause. Other listed prepositions do not fit.

questions.prompt: Fill gap 3 with the correct form of light.
questions.explanation: The replacement is lighter/more light than the earlier ball. Lightest is superlative and more lighter doubled; unlisted plain readings remain reviewable.

questions.prompt: Fill gap 4 with one appropriate word.
questions.explanation: Symbol is subject antecedent of that/which appeared. Who is human, where not subject and what incompatible with the antecedent.

questions.prompt: Fill gap 5 with the correct form of watch.
questions.explanation: Suggested watching uses -ing; the listed base/past/to-infinitive forms do not follow suggested directly.

questions.prompt: Fill gap 6 with the correct form of turn.
questions.explanation: Each of my turns refers to multiple attempts, turns. Turning is not the count noun here; unlisted singular is reviewable.

questions.prompt: Fill gap 7 with the correct form of they.
questions.explanation: Their modifies help. Personal and independent possessive forms do not fit.

questions.prompt: Fill gap 8 with the correct form of prepare.
questions.explanation: Singular lane receives preparation. Ongoing/simple past passive fit; prepared lacks auxiliary and were disagrees.

questions.prompt: Fill gap 9 with one appropriate word.
questions.explanation: A better idea begins with consonant b. Other article readings remain reviewable.

questions.prompt: Fill gap 10 with the correct form of try.
questions.explanation: Looked forward to takes a noun/-ing clause, trying. Other listed forms do not fit the preposition.

units.title: The pages in the wrong order
units.alignmentNote: Complete original ten-gap passage with seven supplied-word and three one-word gaps. Source is a level/family reference only.

materials.title: The pages in the wrong order
materials.text:
Our class made a picture book for younger pupils. Each pair of students created one page, and our teacher asked us ____1____ (bring) the pages together on Friday. We had planned the story, but had not yet seen the whole book.

At first, the pictures looked wonderful. Then we read the story aloud and found a problem. A character thanked her friend before the friend had helped ____2____ (she). Two pages were in the wrong order.

We put the sheets on the floor and gave each one ____3____ number. Moving the pages was easy before they were joined. It would have been much ____4____ (hard) after the cover was attached.

One picture showed a blue bag, while the next showed a green one. The same character carried it, so we decided to make the colour consistent. Another page contained a word ____5____ the youngest readers might not know. We added a clear picture clue rather than simply telling them to guess.

After ____6____ (check) the order, we invited a younger pupil to listen. He laughed at the ending, but asked why the dog had suddenly disappeared. We had forgotten to show it leaving the room. A small change to the final two ____7____ (picture) made that part easier to follow.

The pages ____8____ (join) by our teacher after everyone had agreed on the final version. We kept a copy of the plan ____9____ our folder. The finished book looked simple, but its ____10____ (simple) came from many small decisions about what a new reader needed to see.

questions.prompt: Fill gap 1 with the correct form of bring.
questions.explanation: Asked us takes to bring. Other listed forms do not fit directly.

questions.prompt: Fill gap 2 with the correct form of she.
questions.explanation: Helped takes object her for the other person. She/hers are not object forms and herself would refer back to the friend rather than the character.

questions.prompt: Fill gap 3 with one appropriate word.
questions.explanation: A number begins with consonant n. Other article readings remain reviewable.

questions.prompt: Fill gap 4 with the correct form of hard.
questions.explanation: Much harder/more hard gives the increased difficulty after binding. Hardest is superlative and more harder doubled.

questions.prompt: Fill gap 5 with one appropriate word.
questions.explanation: Word is object of that/which the readers might not know. Who is human, where not object and whose needs a possessed noun.

questions.prompt: Fill gap 6 with the correct form of check.
questions.explanation: After checking/having checked both express prior action. Other listed forms do not directly fit.

questions.prompt: Fill gap 7 with the correct form of picture.
questions.explanation: Two requires plural pictures. Singular and participle do not fill the count slot.

questions.prompt: Fill gap 8 with the correct form of join.
questions.explanation: Plural pages receive joining, so were/had been joined. Joined lacks auxiliary and was disagrees.

questions.prompt: Fill gap 9 with one appropriate word.
questions.explanation: A plan kept in a folder is contained there. To/of/from do not express that storage location.

questions.prompt: Fill gap 10 with the correct form of simple.
questions.explanation: Its simplicity requires a noun. Simple is adjective and simply adverb.

units.title: The model we could touch
units.alignmentNote: Complete original ten-gap passage with seven supplied-word and three one-word gaps. Source is a level/family reference only.

materials.title: The model we could touch
materials.text:
At a museum visit, our group was shown a model of a historic building. Unlike the original object in the display case, this model could be touched under the guide's instructions. It ____1____ (make) to help visitors explore the arrangement of the building in another way.

The guide asked us to notice the difference ____2____ the model and the original. The model was smaller, used different materials and left out some details. Those choices did not make it pointless; they made its purpose easier ____3____ (understand).

One classmate followed a raised line from the entrance to the courtyard. Another noticed steps ____4____ were difficult to see in the photograph beside the case. The model and picture offered different kinds of information about the same place.

We were asked not to assume that a clear model told the whole history. It showed a selected arrangement at a particular period. Earlier repairs and later changes required further ____5____ (explain), which the guide provided with separate images.

After ____6____ (examine) the model, we wrote short descriptions without looking at our notes. I remembered the courtyard ____7____ (clear) than the decoration on the roof. My classmate remembered a different feature, so we compared what had drawn our attention.

The activity gave ____8____ (we) a useful question for future visits: what does this representation help us notice, and what might it leave out? We thanked the guide ____9____ making the comparison practical. A museum label could describe access in general terms, but the model showed us ____10____ (direct) how one object could support more than one way of learning.

questions.prompt: Fill gap 1 with the correct form of make.
questions.explanation: Singular model receives making. Was/had been made fit; made lacks auxiliary and were disagrees.

questions.prompt: Fill gap 2 with one appropriate word.
questions.explanation: Difference between two identified objects uses between. Among suggests a larger set and from does not complete this noun phrase directly.

questions.prompt: Fill gap 3 with the correct form of understand.
questions.explanation: Easier to understand takes an infinitive. Other listed forms do not fit directly.

questions.prompt: Fill gap 4 with one appropriate word.
questions.explanation: Steps are subject antecedent of that/which were difficult. Who is human, where not subject and what incompatible with the antecedent.

questions.prompt: Fill gap 5 with the correct form of explain.
questions.explanation: Further explanation can be general, explanations several accounts. Verb/adjective do not fit the noun slot.

questions.prompt: Fill gap 6 with the correct form of examine.
questions.explanation: After examining/having examined expresses prior examination. Other listed forms do not fit directly.

questions.prompt: Fill gap 7 with the correct form of clear.
questions.explanation: More clearly modifies remembered; flat-adverb clearer is also accepted. Most clearly is superlative and more clearer doubled.

questions.prompt: Fill gap 8 with the correct form of we.
questions.explanation: Gave takes object us. Subject and possessive forms do not fit.

questions.prompt: Fill gap 9 with one appropriate word.
questions.explanation: Thanked the guide for making uses for. Other listed prepositions do not fit.

questions.prompt: Fill gap 10 with the correct form of direct.
questions.explanation: Directly modifies showed. Direction is noun; unlisted flat-adverb uses remain reviewable.

materials.title: The cover that changed the reading
materials.text:
The art club designed two possible covers for our school magazine. One showed a large sports photograph; the other used a pattern made from small images of many activities. The editor asked us ____1____ (compare) them with the contents rather than voting only for our favourite colour.

The issue contained one sports report, two stories, an interview and several reviews. A cover ____2____ suggested that every page was about sport could give a misleading first impression. The photograph was attractive, but attraction was not the only consideration.

We also checked the title's ____3____ (visible). Some letters disappeared against the dark part of the photograph. Making them larger did not solve every problem, so we tried a different position and a clearer background.

The second design included more activities, ____4____ its small pictures were difficult to recognise at the size of the printed magazine. A cover viewed on a large screen did not behave exactly like a copy held in the hand.

Before ____5____ (choose), we printed small test versions. The editor showed them to students who had not worked on the issue. They asked several ____6____ (question) that helped us identify what each cover seemed to promise.

In the end, we selected a revised design with fewer, ____7____ (large) images and a clear title. The final file ____8____ (save) separately from the drafts, so the printer would receive the correct version. We kept the earlier designs ____9____ our project record. They showed why the choices had changed, not simply which cover had won. The discussion made ____10____ (we) think of a cover as a guide into the magazine, rather than a prize awarded to the most striking picture.

questions.prompt: Fill gap 1 with the correct form of compare.
questions.explanation: Asked us takes to compare. Other listed forms do not directly fit.

questions.prompt: Fill gap 2 with one appropriate word.
questions.explanation: Cover is subject antecedent of that/which suggested. Who is human, where not subject and what incompatible with the antecedent.

questions.prompt: Fill gap 3 with the correct form of visible.
questions.explanation: The title’s visibility requires a noun. Visible is adjective and visibly adverb.

questions.prompt: Fill gap 4 with one appropriate word.
questions.explanation: But/yet express contrast; although/though can introduce the following concession. Unless introduces an unprovided condition rather than the observed small-picture problem.

questions.prompt: Fill gap 5 with the correct form of choose.
questions.explanation: Before choosing takes an -ing clause after the preposition. Other listed forms do not fit directly.

questions.prompt: Fill gap 6 with the correct form of question.
questions.explanation: Several requires plural count noun questions. Singular question and the activity noun questioning do not fit this explicit count slot.

questions.prompt: Fill gap 7 with the correct form of large.
questions.explanation: Fewer, larger images contrasts the previous many small ones. Largest is superlative and more larger doubled; plain large remains reviewable.

questions.prompt: Fill gap 8 with the correct form of save.
questions.explanation: Singular file receives saving, so was/had been saved. Saved lacks auxiliary and were disagrees.

questions.prompt: Fill gap 9 with one appropriate word.
questions.explanation: In our project record expresses inclusion in the saved record. Other listed prepositions do not express that storage relation.

questions.prompt: Fill gap 10 with the correct form of we.
questions.explanation: Made takes object us. Subject and possessive forms do not fit.
